standards.title: Murabahah Policy Document
standards.applicability: Islamic banks, takaful operators, FSA banks with Islamic windows, DFIA prescribed institutions
key_rulings: 10.1 Definition: sale of asset with acquisition cost and mark-up disclosed to purchaser.
11.1 Binding sale; no unilateral termination.
13.1 Asset must exist and be owned by seller; 13.3 bans assets under construction and debt-type assets.
13.4 Ribawi asset rules: no same-type/category murabahah; no deferred same-category different-type.
13.6-13.8 Ownership transfers on valid contract even without legal registration; possession = qabd haqiqi or hukmi.
13.11 No multiple simultaneous murabahah on same asset.
14.2-14.4 Price = disclosed cost + mark-up; mark-up may reference BLR/BFR/KLIBOR/COF but reference rate must be specified.
14.6 Indirect expenses (rent, wages, utilities) excluded from acquisition cost.
14.13 Rescheduling allowed with NO increase of remaining debt.

15.1-15.7 MPO: wa'd binding once seller acts to acquire; wa'd executed separately BEFORE murabahah; breach = compensation for actual costs + disposal shortfall; murabahah must not precede seller's purchase.
16.2 Wakalah (customer as purchasing agent) must be documented separately from murabahah.
17.6 Collateral must be Shariah-compliant asset; 17.7 conventional fixed deposit acceptable as collateral valued to principal only.
17.10-17.14 Hamish jiddiyah: compensate actual loss only, excess returned.
17.15-17.17 'Urbun: kept by seller if option not exercised.
18.2 Ibra' clause mandatory when required by authority.
19.2 Late charges: ta'widh (actual loss, income) + gharamah (penalty, NOT income — to charity).
App1: legitimacy — Quran 2:275; no direct Sunnah authority (general permissibility of sale); ijma'; qiyas on tawliyah.

standards.title: Wa`d Policy Document
standards.applicability: Islamic banks, takaful/retakaful operators, FSA Islamic-window banks, DFIA prescribed institutions

divergence_evidence.position: Malaysia/BNM: wa'd attached to condition/time/price/conduct/event IS BINDING on promisor from date made (9.2-9.3); promisee may claim ACTUAL loss (12.3-12.4); muwa'adah (bilateral) also binding and enforceable (15.2) but currency muwa'adah only for hedging (15.5).

key_rulings: 8.1 Wa'd = unilateral promise; 9.1 not a contract.
9.2-9.3 Binding when attached to condition/time/price/conduct/event; binding from the date made.
11.5 No counter-value (fee) for the wa'd itself.
12.1-12.4 No unilateral revocation; compensation limited to actual loss, determined by authoritative body or 'urf tijari methodology.
13.5-13.6 Forward currency exchange via wa'd permissible ONLY for hedging.
13.11 Qard borrower must not give wa'd of hibah to lender.
14.3 Revocation only if promisee consents or does not invoke.
15.1-15.5 Muwa'adah = bilateral promise, binding, not a contract; all wa'd rules apply; currency use = hedging only.
18.7 IFI shall not impose/pay any consideration for wa'd (fees on accompanying contracts OK, 18.8).
18.9-18.11 Actual loss floor: principal shortfall vs recoverable value, acquisition-vs-disposal shortfall, direct costs; estimation must use market methodologies + reliable sources.
18.18-18.19 Currency wa'd (incl. derivatives) must mitigate pre-existing exposure of at least one party; documentary evidence required.
App1: Quran 17:34, 23:8, 61:2-3, 19:54; hadith Muslim 220 (signs of hypocrite).

standards.title: Kafalah Policy Document
standards.effective_note: Part E (submission) immediate; implementation plan due 31 Oct 2016 per 28.2 (date precedes issuance in text — quoted as printed)
standards.applicability: Islamic banks, takaful/retakaful (Part B only), FSA Islamic-window banks, DFIA prescribed institutions

divergence_evidence.position: Malaysia/BNM: guarantor MAY impose a fee for the kafalah service — fixed amount or percentage of guaranteed amount (15.1-15.2). If a fee is paid, kafalah cannot be dissolved without guaranteed party's consent (18.2).

key_rulings: 8.1 Definition: guarantor conjoins guaranteed party in assuming specified liability; 9.2 binding on guarantor.
1.7 Scope limited to financial guarantee (kafalah bi al-mal); kafalah al-nafs/al-wajh excluded.
13.1 Subject matter must not arise from Shariah non-compliant contracts/activities.
14.1-14.5 Unrestricted vs restricted kafalah; restricted terms must be consistent with original liability.
14.6-14.7 Beneficiary may claim from either party; guarantor may stipulate claim-debtor-first condition.
15.1-15.2 FEE PERMITTED: fixed or % of guaranteed amount.
16.1-16.5 Recourse against guaranteed party even for voluntary kafalah; capped at amount paid (16.2) but total costs recoverable (16.3); set-off allowed.
16.7 Defaulting guarantor faces same actions as guaranteed party.
18.1-18.2 Dissolution by beneficiary discharge; fee-paid kafalah needs guaranteed party consent.
22.5 Kafalah + wakalah must be independent contracts, effects not interrelated.
27.3 IFI as beneficiary should claim guaranteed party first before guarantor (G).
App1: Quran 12:72 (Yusuf); hadith Abu Daud 3343 (Abu Qatadah pays two dinars); ijma' cited via Ibn Qudamah al-Mughni 4:400.

standards.title: Tawarruq Policy Document (reissuance)
standards.applicability: Islamic banks, takaful operators (Part B only), FSA Islamic-window banks, DFIA prescribed institutions

divergence_evidence.position: Malaysia/BNM: organised tawarruq PERMITTED and fully regulated (whole PD). Anti-inah guards: purchaser of first sale must not sell back to original seller (11.2, 18.3); no condition restricting delivery or obliging onward sale (15.5); contracts sequenced and separate (12.3, 15.2); no multiple tawarruq on same asset at one time (13.18); gold/silver/currencies excluded as subject (13.4). Bursa Suq Al-Sila' named as asset exchange (25.5).

key_rulings: 9.1 Definition: two sales — deferred sale then cash/spot sale to third party.
10.3 Each sale may be murabahah or musawamah.
11.2 Seller in sale 1 must NOT be purchaser in sale 2 (no inah).
12.3 Strict sequence of offer/acceptance.
13.4 Excluded assets: gold, silver, currencies; under-construction; debt-type.
13.8-13.10 Purchaser must take possession (haqiqi/hukmi) before onward sale.
13.18 Same asset cannot back multiple tawarruq at once.
14.5 Rescheduling must not increase remaining debt; 14.6-14.7 refinancing new-debt contract only for solvent debtor.
15.5 No terms restricting delivery or obliging purchaser to sell.
15.6 No payment of deferred price before contract entered.
16.15-16.16 Agent holds funds on amanah; qard treatment only by necessity (T+2 processing window per 25.22).
17.1-17.4 Dual agency permitted with upfront agreed essentials + proper sequence + evidence.
18.2-18.3 No condition requiring promise to sell to third party or back to original seller.
25.10 Asset criteria: open-market valuable, contract grade, good condition, active market, not MFRS-intangible.
25.26 Breach-of-promise loss = direct costs only (no overheads/opportunity costs).
26.2 Risk framework incl. inventory risk between the two sales.
App1: Quran 2:275; no direct Sunnah authority — permitted under general permissibility of sale.

standards.title: Qard Policy Document

supersedes.title: wadi'ah yad dhamanah products transition — all such products revised to qard by 2018-07-31 (para 22)

standards.applicability: Islamic banks, takaful/retakaful, FSA Islamic-window banks, DFIA prescribed institutions
key_rulings: 8.1 Definition: lending money; borrower repays equivalent replacement. 8.2 Money incl. cash/gold/silver.
14.1 NO contractual benefit to lender: bans pre-agreed periodic ibra' linked to qard, wa'd-based incentives, conditional hibah (cash/kind/benefit).
14.5-14.8 Borrower hibah to lender only fully discretionary; no promotion of indicative rates; historical hibah disclosure allowed with strict disclaimers (20.5).
14.9 Borrower keeps any benefit/revenue from borrowed money.
14.11 Repayment in different currency at prevailing/agreed rate ON payment date.
15.1-15.7 Ujrah only for services unrelated to the qard; direct-cost charges only for qard-related services; no ujrah on loan extension, late repayment, or cash-back exchange.
15A Bai' wa salaf (qard + exchange contract) prohibited if inter-conditional or gives lender exclusive benefit.
22 Transition: wadi'ah yad dhamanah → qard by 31 Jul 2018; product names must drop 'wadi'ah'/'safekeeping' terms (22.5).
App1: Quran 2:245; hadith Ibn Majah 2421, Bukhari 2212; ijma'.

standards.title: Hibah Policy Document
standards.applicability: Islamic banks, takaful/retakaful, FSA Islamic-window banks, DFIA prescribed institutions
key_rulings: 8.1 Definition: transfer of asset ownership donor→recipient without consideration; 9.1 benevolent (tabarru') contract.
9.2-9.3 Revocable before possession/condition-fulfilment; father→child hibah revocable anytime except transfer to third party or encumbrance.
13.2-13.3 Asset must exist and be owned by donor; future-received asset allowed (13.3); minor's asset cannot be hibah (13.4).
14.4-14.5 Hibah lapses into donor's estate on death before possession, EXCEPT hibah conditional on donor's death → takaful only (15.3).
14.6 Effect permanent; time-limiting condition void.
16.1-16.4 With ijarah (IMB): via wa'd mulzim or conditional hibah; hibah documented separately from ijarah.
17.2/18.2/19.3 With mudarabah/musharakah/wakalah-istithmar: hibah must not come from capital or the other party's profit share, and must not amount to capital/profit guarantee.
20.2-20.5 With qard: no conditional hibah to lender; discretion-only; no indicative-rate marketing.
App1: Quran 4:4; hadith al-Baihaqi 11726 ('exchange gifts'); ijma'.

standards.title: Wakalah Policy Document
standards.applicability: Islamic banks, FSA Islamic-window banks, takaful/retakaful, DFIA prescribed institutions; investment-account use governed by Investment Account PD (2.2)
key_rulings: 8.1 Definition: principal authorises agent for delegable task, with or without fee.
9.2 Binding when: third-party rights involved; fee-based; work commenced with damage on stop; agreed no-termination window.
11.5/16.1-16.3 Fuduli (unauthorised agent) transactions ratifiable under set conditions; otherwise rescinded.
14.1-14.2 Disclosed vs undisclosed agency: rights/liabilities fall on principal vs agent respectively (hukm binds principal either way).
14.3-14.6 Dual agency permitted incl. self-dealing as counterparty (tawarruq deposit/financing) with upfront determination + all principals' consent.
14.11 Agent liable only on ta'addi/taqsir/mukhalafah al-shurut.
15.2-15.8 Fee rules; ujrah al-mithl when rate undetermined but work done.
18.3(c) Agent must not guarantee own performance nor capital/return under wakalah bi al-istithmar.
20.2-20.7 Investment wakalah: no capital/return guarantee; breach → repay capital + actual profit to breach + compensation; independent third-party (non-related) capital guarantee allowed.
20.9-20.10 Hibah to cover shortfall vs expected profit allowed but never obligatory.
21.1 Dissolution events incl. death/loss of capacity/loss of subject matter.
App1: Quran 18:19; hadith Bukhari 3370 ('Urwah's dinar), Abu Dawud 3148; ijma'.

standards.title: Rahn Policy Document
standards.applicability: Islamic banks, takaful/retakaful, FSA Islamic-window banks, DFIA prescribed institutions
key_rulings: 8.1 Definition: pledgor pledges asset as collateral to pledgee for obligor's liability in default event; 9.2 binding on pledgor.
14.1-14.2 Collateral may be physical (even non-Shariah-use) or financial; mixed financial asset needs Shariah-compliant core business; non-compliant financial asset capped at principal value.
14.4 Future asset may be pledged.
14.12 Multiple pledgees: pari passu with consent, or ranked with succeeding pledgee's consent.
15.3 Pledgee may utilise collateral only with owner consent, NOT for qard-sourced liability, terms+period specified.
16.1-16.3 Maintenance costs on owner; other rahn costs on pledgor unless agreed.
17.5 Mixed financial asset liquidation: segregable → Shariah-compliant proceeds only.
17.7-17.9 Shortfall stays obligor's liability; excess returned to owner.
19.1 Rahn may attach to murabahah, tawarruq, bai' 'inah (noted as permitted arrangement in MY).
23.1-23.2 In mudarabah/musharakah/wakalah-istithmar: collateral must NOT guarantee capital/profit; liquidation only on misconduct/negligence/breach.
26.1-26.4 Dissolution events; death does not dissolve — heirs assume.
31.3(b) Islamic pawnbroking = qard secured by safekept collateral with fee.
App1: Quran 2:283; hadith Bukhari/Muslim (armour pledged to Jew); ijma' via Ibn Qudamah al-Mughni 4/362.

standards.title: Bai` al-Sarf (Currency Exchange) Policy Document
standards.applicability: IFIs offering currency-note/coin exchange (excludes gold/silver, 2.1); money services business: Part B + para 25 only

divergence_evidence.position: Malaysia/BNM: money-for-money exchange must complete delivery+possession within contract session (14.1); same currency at par (14.5); different currency any agreed rate (14.6); extension beyond session only for 'urf-established operational constraint or unexpected disruption (14.4); 'urbun and khiyar al-shart banned in sarf (14.3); wa'd/wa'dan/muwa'adah forward arrangements ONLY for hedging (16.4); debt payable in different currency at rate on payment date, never pre-agreed (18.3).

key_rulings: 8.1-8.3 Definition: exchange money for money, same or different type.
9.1 Binding; no unilateral termination (except khiyar al-'ayb 19.1(b)).
14.1-14.2 Spot possession within contract session (session ends by disengagement or takhayur waiver).
14.5 Same currency = par; 14.6 different = agreed rate.
16.1-16.4 Wa'd / two wa'dan / muwa'adah forwards allowed for hedging only.
17.1-17.4 May combine with ijarah al-khadamat (remittance etc.) in one document if contracts distinguished; service fee allowed.
18.1-18.3 Cross-currency debt settlement/set-off at payment-date rate.
22.7 Ringgit pairs use onshore-fixed reference rate.
App1: Quran 2:275; hadith Muslim 2970 (six ribawi items) — 'illah thamaniyyah extends gold/silver rules to modern currencies.

standards.title: Wadi`ah Policy Document
standards.applicability: Islamic banks, takaful/retakaful, FSA Islamic-window banks, DFIA prescribed institutions
key_rulings: 8.1 Definition: asset placed with another party for safekeeping; 9.1 nature = trusteeship (yad amanah), unilaterally terminable.
14.5 Custodian not liable for loss except own/agents' ta'addi, taqsir, mukhalafah al-shurut.
14.6-14.8 No third-party custody without depositor permission; breach = full liability.
15.1-15.3 Charging a safekeeping fee TRANSFORMS the contract into ijarah, with lessor-level liability.
16.1 KEY: wadi'ah of fungible asset (money) + permission to utilise = CONSTRUED AS QARD, governed by qard rules.
18.1 Dissolution incl. unilateral termination, death/dissolution, ownership change.
22.1 Late collection: fee/direct costs chargeable or surrender to authorities.
27.1-27.2 Transition to qard PD; utilised money placements must be called qard.
App1: Quran 23:8, 4:58, 2:283; hadith al-Baihaqi 12696, Abu Daud 3535; ijma'.

standards.title: Mudarabah Policy Document
standards.effective_note: Part B immediate on issuance; Parts C/D operational from 2016-06-01

supersedes.title: Guidelines on Musharakah and Mudarabah contracts for Islamic Banking Institutions (mudarabah requirements)

standards.applicability: Islamic banks, takaful operators (Part B only), FSA Islamic-window banks, DFIA prescribed institutions; excludes sukuk/CIS/equities, interbank investments excluded from Part D
standards.reading_scope: Parts A+B + Part C through 25.18 verified; remainder of Part C/D (risk mgmt, Part D rabbul-mal ops, appendices) not yet read — say the word to finish.
key_rulings: 10.1 Definition: capital provider + entrepreneur; profit by agreed PSR; losses borne by rabbul mal unless mudarib's ta'addi/taqsir/mukhalafah.
11.1 Fiduciary (aqd al-amanah); 11.2 unilateral termination barred once work commenced / fixed term agreed.
11.3 Mutlaqah vs muqayyadah.
14.4 Mudarib yudarib / agent assignment needs rabbul mal consent; 14.5 rabbul mal excluded from management but has information rights.
15.4-15.7 Capital cash or in-kind (valued); DEBT cannot be capital; 25.8 operationally capital must be cash only, not encumbered.
15.10 No capital guarantee by mudarib.
15.14 Mudarib fund injection → musharakah forms with the venture.
16.3-16.9 No profit guarantee; PSR at inception, revisable by mutual agreement; no pre-fixed lump profit; profit not a % of capital.
16.11 Multi-tier mudarabah PSR per tier.
16.16 Profit recognition: actual liquidation (haqiqi) or constructive (hukmi) with final true-up (16.18).
17.1-17.5 Loss to rabbul mal up to capital; multiple rabbul mal bear pro-rata.
18.2-18.3 Collateral liquidation only on misconduct/negligence/breach; independent (non-related) third-party guarantee of capital allowed, separate contract.
20.2 Hibah by mudarib not from capital/rabbul-mal profit, no guarantee effect.
21.1-21.2 Wa'd by mudarib to buy mudarabah asset on trigger events; price at market/fair/agreed-at-purchase.
22.1 Dissolution events incl. death/dissolution, loss of capacity, invalidity.

standards.title: Istisna` Policy Document
standards.applicability: Islamic banks + takaful operators, FSA Islamic-window banks, DFIA prescribed institutions; IFI as seller or purchaser
standards.reading_scope: Parts A+B fully verified; Part C read through 35.5; tail (35.6-36 + appendices 3-6) not yet read.
key_rulings: 9.1 Definition: sale of asset yet to be constructed/built/manufactured to agreed specs, future delivery, pre-determined price.
10.2 Binding once specs + price/time/place/mode fixed; 30.1 no unilateral dissolution.
14.5 An existing identifiable completed asset cannot be the istisna' asset.
15.1-15.5 Ownership with seller until delivery; purchaser cannot on-sell before possession (except as-is possession agreement 15.6).
16.1-16.6 Price fixed at inception; revision cases (cost fall/rise, spec change); NO upward revision for payment-period extension (16.6).
17.7 Late delivery → purchaser claims actual loss.
17.15-17.17 Non-completion: as-is possession (pay to stage) or dissolve (full refund + compensation).
17.18/18.1 Seller cannot waive liability for completion or material defects.
27.2 Late payment charges: ta'widh income-able; gharamah to charity/Baitulmal; 27.4 shart jaza'i (late-delivery charge) may be income to PURCHASER.
28.1-28.3 Parallel istisna': two separate independent contracts, obligations independent.
26.1-26.2 Forward lease (ijarah mawsufah fi al-zimmah) on asset under construction — separate contract.
30.2-30.9 Dissolution options incl. khiyar fawat al-wasf; on seller death purchaser may take as-is or dissolve; purchaser death does NOT dissolve (30.6).

standards.title: Ijarah Policy Document
standards.applicability: IFIs offering ijarah products other than capital market instruments; takaful operators Part B only; incorporates Hire-Purchase Act 1967 protections for repossession (1.9)
standards.reading_scope: Parts A+B fully verified; Part C read through 30.28; Parts C-tail/D/E + appendices not yet read.
key_rulings: 8.1 Definition: transfer of usufruct ownership for period for consideration (asset lease; service hire excluded from this PD 9.2).
9.4 Binding contract.
13.1 Asset/usufruct: Shariah-recognised, valuable, existing, identifiable, accessible, deliverable, not debt-based, non-perishable; existence waived for mawsufah fi zimmah (13.2).
13.10 No simultaneous lease of one asset in 2+ ijarah.
13.12 Sale of leased asset to third party transfers lessor's rights/liabilities; uninformed buyer may rescind.
14.4 Benchmark-linked rental needs min-max limits; 14.5 no unilateral rental increase.
16.1-16.2 Ownership risks + maintenance-of-usufruct costs on lessor; usage liabilities on lessee.
16.3-16.6 Lessee liable only on misconduct/negligence/breach; force majeure restoration on lessor.
16.7/16.7A Takaful protection mandatory; conventional insurance only if takaful unavailable/rejected/significantly costlier.
18.1-18.5 Sub-lease allowed unless barred; period within head lease.
19.3 Lease-leaseback: separate independent contracts, no wa'd to leaseback, no pre-signing, no arranged-sequence references.
20.1-20.10 Forward ijarah (mawsufah fi zimmah / mudafah ila mustaqbal); non-delivery → all paid rentals returned.
21.2 Sale-and-leaseback: sale concluded first, separate docs, leaseback not a condition of sale.
22.1-22.11 IMB: transfer by sale / conditional hibah / wa'd-to-hibah; wa'd-to-purchase triggered only on default or breach (22.5); collateral-liquidation waterfall with excess to lessee (22.10).
30.4 Early settlement/default ownership-transfer mechanism must be wa'd to purchase by customer.
26.2-26.4 Ta'widh income-able; gharamah to Baitulmal/charity.

standards.duplicate_files_note: Two identical copies on disk: 'Shariah Governance Policy Document 2019.txt' and 'Bank Negra Shariah Governance Policy Document 2019.txt' — same doc (both read; identical content). Archive one.
key_rulings: 11.2 Shariah committee meets ≥ once per 2 months (windows/foreign branches ≥2/yr, 11.3).
12.1-12.2 Member criteria: Muslim, fit & proper, Shariah-qualified (bachelor Shariah w/ Usul Fiqh or Fiqh Muamalat) or supporting expert.

13.2-13.3 ≥5 members, majority + chairman Shariah-qualified.
16.3 Control functions: Shariah risk management, Shariah review, Shariah audit.
22.9 Annual-report Shariah compliance opinion wording prescribed.
